label: SIMULATION

releases.rule: DR1 and QR3 are one uniformly processed set. QR2 used the previous gain: combine only after the L3 flux corrections.

dr1.note: Reprocessed; forms one uniformly processed set with QR3. Use for new work.

qr3.note: New gain calibration; uniform with DR1.

qr2.note: Superseded. Not searchable; direct download through February 2027. Previous gain: needs the L3 flux corrections before any comparison with QR3 or DR1.

calibration_impact.stage: Raw difference. Pixel grids laid on top, no alignment.
Aligned with the WCS of each file.
Sky level removed and star gain matched.
Honest noise: measured noise factor and the resampling error of stars.
Fair co adds of the whole visit, matched colors.
Detections of three methods (P, D, A)
Surviving sky candidates (engine says sky and forensics clean)

validation.chance_note: Mean false candidates per empty simulated field (40 null fields). Compare with the count here.

static_stars.meaning: Catalog stars with no motion that the motion court calls moving.

null_twin.meaning: The same field with every planted change removed. Each candidate here is a false alarm.

time_shuffle.meaning: Visit times shuffled for every moving source. A real motion loses its fit when time order is broken.

alignment_stress.meaning: Spots above 5 sigma in the fair pairs when only the file WCS aligns the images, after the star anchors, and in the final fair co adds.

real_vs_simulated.lesson: Simulated performance does not predict real performance. Real QR3 recovery is far lower.

published_pair.falsification: Two positions fit infinitely many orbits. Predict the position for a new epoch; a non detection there, at a depth that should see it, rejects that orbit.
published_pair.status: candidate pair from the literature, not a discovery

selection.model: a 380 to 800 au, e 0.1 to 0.45, uniform mean anomaly, mass 6 Earth, albedo 0.4 (all assumptions)
selection.meaning: Most of a distant orbit is near aphelion, where the planet is faintest: a survey that saw nothing has not searched most of the orbit.

identity: CHRONOS does not merely search for changes. It investigates whether they are real, explains how they could have occurred, and names the evidence that would prove it wrong.
